title: Publish regulated workload landing pages (FinServ + Healthcare) + nav/SEO updates
author: Kira Thompson
commits: docs(landing): add FinServ regulated workloads page content + components
docs(landing): add Healthcare regulated workloads page content + PHI-safe copy
docs(seo): add page-level metadata (title/description/canonical/og) + update sitemap includes
docs(nav): add Regulated Workloads section + cross-links from Security/Compliance
chore: copy edits based on Security + PMM review; tighten retention/residency phrasing
body:
Summary: Publishes two vertical-specific regulated workload landing pages for the ABM pilot (Financial Services + Healthcare) and updates navigation + SEO metadata so the pages are discoverable, indexable, and shareable. This PR is intentionally scoped to content + docs-site wiring; form routing/UTM attribution is handled in product/marketing infra (ENG-2941) and is not part of this change.

Why: The regulated ABM pilot needs credible, security-forward entry points that map to Redwood’s Hosted → Dedicated → Private story without over-promising on compliance or roadmap. These pages are meant to (1) pre-answer common security questions, (2) drive prospects to a security review / Private architecture deep dive, and (3) give AEs/SDRs a stable URL to use in sequences.

What’s included: 1) New landing pages: /regulated/financial-services and /regulated/healthcare. Each page includes a vertical problem framing, workload examples, deployment-model guidance (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and security callouts aligned to current support. 2) Navigation updates: Adds “Regulated Workloads” entry under Solutions and adds contextual cross-links from Security/Compliance pages. 3) SEO/social metadata: Title/description/canonical + OpenGraph/Twitter cards; ensures pages are included in sitemap generation.

Copy guardrails (applied): - Avoids claiming certifications not guaranteed for all deployments (no “HIPAA certified” / no “PCI compliant out of the box”). - Uses approved phrasing for retention/residency (e.g., “configurable retention controls by deployment mode” and “data residency options depend on selected region / Private deployment topology”). - Healthcare page uses PHI-safe language and explicitly scopes assumptions (customer controls PHI ingestion patterns; Redwood can support Private/VPC/on-prem patterns for regulated data).

Notable implementation details: - Introduced shared components for the hero + deployment chooser to keep layout consistent and reduce future edits. - Centralized per-page metadata in a small helper so marketing can adjust title/description without hunting through MDX frontmatter conventions.

Rollout checklist: - [x] Preview links shared with PMM + Security for final pass (see review thread). - [x] Confirm canonical URLs match final paths (/regulated/financial-services, /regulated/healthcare). - [x] Confirm sitemap includes new routes and robots.txt remains unchanged (index enabled). - [x] Confirm no references to unreleased features; copy matches Security/GRC-approved language. - [ ] After merge: coordinate with Growth to update email sequences + HubSpot CTAs to use final URLs (owner: Ben Carter). - [ ] After merge: add redirects from any previously shared preview/slugs if needed (owner: Elliot Price).

Screenshots/Preview: Vercel preview is attached in checks. Please test on mobile widths; the deployment chooser collapses into a single-column layout.

Notes: This PR intentionally does not add gated content or PDF downloads. If we decide to gate in week 3–4 of the pilot, we can layer that on via marketing ops without changing these routes.
review_conversation: Soojin Lee: Copy looks strong. Request: tighten the FinServ proof points so we don’t imply we’ve completed specific bank audits. Also please make the CTA consistent (“Schedule a security review” vs “Talk to an engineer”).

Kira Thompson (author): Updated proof points to be outcome/feature based (audit logging, KMS/HSM integration points, VPC/on-prem options) and standardized CTA to “Schedule a security review” with secondary “Request a Private architecture review.”

Marcus Lin: On Healthcare page, remove “BAA available” unless we’re certain we can execute quickly; suggest “BAA available as part of enterprise contracting (as applicable)” and avoid timing commitments.

Kira Thompson (author): Updated to “BAA available as part of enterprise contracting (as applicable)” and removed timeline language. Also added a short scoping note: we’ll confirm BAA/DPA requirements during security review.

Naomi Feldman: SEO metadata: ensure we don’t put “HIPAA” in title tag unless it’s clearly a capability statement, not a certification. Also confirm the retention language matches the internal guidance (“may vary by deployment mode”).

Kira Thompson (author): Adjusted title tag from “HIPAA” phrasing to “Healthcare regulated workloads” and updated retention copy to “retention controls vary by deployment mode and customer configuration.”
Elliot Price: Nav placement looks good. Please add a short blurb/link from the Security page to the regulated pages and run link-check again; we’ve had relative-link regressions recently.
Kira Thompson (author): Added cross-link cards from Security + Compliance index pages and re-ran link-check; all green.
Elliot Price: Approved. Please file a follow-up for redirects if any old draft URLs are in outbound sequences already.
Kira Thompson (author): Follow-up noted in rollout checklist; Ben/Elliot coordinating with Growth on final URL swap.
release_notes: Docs: Added new regulated workload landing pages for Financial Services and Healthcare, including updated navigation and SEO metadata for discoverability.
